cases.note: §43's own example, declared: two arms 1.2 m apart, each confined to its half of the bench. Both layers are named for their robot, both are in that robot's own root frame — `at` exists for the disjointness test and for nothing else — and the placed boxes do not meet, so nothing is refused.

A cell with one robot is §55.2's cell. There is no pair to be disjoint from, so the placement and disjointness rules do not apply and a cell naming its single robot without saying where it stands is complete. An edition that applied the rules from the first robot would refuse every cell anybody has written.

The case the section exists for. Each arm is confined, both are placed, and the placed boxes intersect — so two bodies can be in one place and §87.1 has just given them two kernels, neither of which can see the other's envelope. Reported as a claim the platform cannot enforce rather than as a hazard it measured.

cases.note: A shared boundary is a shared point, so the test is inclusive. `margin` counts zero as inside — a workspace trip is `margin < 0` — so both arms may legally be at the millimetre where these boxes meet. cases.note: The sphere pair, disjoint: centres 1.2 m apart and radii summing to 0.6. The one case where an edition comparing squared distances against an unsquared sum would still agree is the one where the answer is the same either way, so this case and the next are a pair.

Centres 1.2 m apart, radii 0.6 each. Exactly touching, and therefore sharing a point — the inclusive rule again, on the arithmetic where an off-by-one hides in a comparison operator rather than in a loop.

cases.note: `env.robot` answers *which robot does this cell say I am*, so a caller asking about a slug the cell has not been told about gets the empty string rather than the slug it asked for. An edition echoing the argument back would let a precondition assert membership of a cell by asserting it.

Every cell written before §87. `env.robots` is empty, `env.robot` is the empty string whatever the caller asked, no layer is contributed, and nothing is refused — which is the property that makes this field additive.

`robot` and `robots` join `cell` and `fixtures` as derived, so a fact of either name would be read by nobody and would make a precondition true for the wrong reason. Both are reported, in sorted key order.
